_comment: Authoritative per-agent spawn-time prompt-inventory budgets, enforced by scripts/check-token-budget.sh. Weight = agent .md + every frontmatter-preloaded SKILL.md, measured as an OFFLINE PROXY (bytes / proxy_bytes_per_token). This is NOT an Anthropic token count and does NOT track live tokenizer inflation — it is a ratchet on prompt inventory growth only. ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACTS.md §'Prompt Token Budgets' mirrors this file for humans; THIS JSON is the single source of truth the gate reads. Keys are agent filename stems (loomwright/agents/<stem>.md). NOTE: the gate consumes ONLY .agents[<stem>].budget — the `measured` and `note` fields (including the '... N preloaded skills' counts in each note) are DECORATIVE, FROZEN authoring-time metadata the gate never re-derives or asserts (do not chase or re-bump them each release; they are authoring snapshots, like CLAUDE.md's frozen-example-value convention). The live preloaded-skill count IS computed and printed per run, but is not gated against these notes. The proxy sizes the whole .md/SKILL.md incl. frontmatter — a deliberate, safe over-count, not the literal system prompt.
proxy_label: proxy tokens (bytes/4 — offline proxy, not an exact Anthropic count)
raise_rule: To raise a budget, edit its .agents[<stem>].budget here in the SAME PR that breaches it and add a one-line justification to that agent's `note`, AND update the mirrored row in ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACTS.md §'Prompt Token Budgets' in the same edit (machine-enforced: the gate asserts each table budget cell equals this JSON; drifted/missing/ghost rows fail CI closed). The gate reads this JSON, so every raise is visible in the PR diff and reviewable. Budgets are a ratchet against unmeasured growth, not a hard diet — shrinking prompts is separate follow-up work. Initial budgets = measured proxy value at authoring time (v15.10.0) + ~10% headroom, so no agent fails at introduction.

supervisor.note: Re-baselined 51814 -> 21029 (4f, v15.19.0): routed all 7 frontmatter-preloaded skills out of loomwright:supervisor-runner's `skills:` list (now 0 preloaded skills — the key is omitted entirely) in favor of on-demand phase-entry Reads for the 3 genuinely needed (async-orchestration at Phase 2 + refreshed at Phase 4, commit at Phase 4, state-management at Phase 4.5) and outright removal of the other 4 (workflow-management, context-summarization, supervisor-readiness, quality-checklist — zero body usage found on audit; see agents/supervisor.md §"Preloaded Skill Routing (4f)"). This is a structural re-baseline (a large drop), not a marginal raise, so the initial-budget convention applies here rather than the compressed-margin convention this row's prior restores used (~1.45%/~1.5%, both explicitly chosen to avoid resetting to a fresh measured+10% after a marginal raise) — the two conventions exist for different situations, and this one is the re-baseline case, not the marginal-raise case. Budget set to measured + ~10% (20591 * 1.10 = 22650.1, rounded up to 22651), restoring genuine headroom after the drop rather than inheriting the prior ~1.45% margin against a now-much-smaller measured value. FINAL-MEASURE NOTE (recorded at end of PR, deliberately not re-raised): the 22651 budget was computed from the FIRST post-routing measure (20591 + ~10% = 22650.1 -> 22651). Later edits inside this same PR — the Phase 4.5 heal commit and an added paragraph clarifying that the re-baseline is spawn-time frontmatter weight rather than a session total — moved measured to 21029, so the realized margin is ~7.7%, not the ~10% the sentence above describes at the moment the budget was chosen. The budget is NOT re-raised for this: the gate compares live weight against budget only and is not breached (1622 proxy tokens of headroom), and chasing every in-PR edit with a fresh raise is exactly the treadmill the frozen-metadata convention exists to avoid. The measured field here is the live end-of-PR value, not the mid-PR one.
